{{nihongo|'''Miyake Shrine (Matsubara)'''|屯倉神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

'''Miyake Shrine'''（みやけじんじゃ）is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Miyakenaka, {{ill|Matsubara|ar|ماتسوبارا (أوساكا)|arz|ماتسوبارا|ca|Matsubara|ce|Мацубара|ceb|Matsubara-shi|de|Matsubara|eo|Macubara|es|Matsubara|fa|ماتسوبارا، اوساکا|fi|Matsubara|fr|Matsubara (Osaka)|gl|Matsubara|hy|Մացուբարա|it|Matsubara|ja|松原市|ko|마쓰바라시|mzn|ماتسوبارا، اوساکا|nl|Matsubara|no|Matsubara|pl|Matsubara|pt|Matsubara|ro|Matsubara|ru|Мацубара|sh|Matsubara|sr|Мацубара|sv|Matsubara|szl|Matsubara|tg|Матсубара|th|มัตสึบาระ (จังหวัดโอซากะ)|tl|Matsubara, Osaka|tr|Matsubara|tt|Мацубара|uk|Мацубара|ur|ماٹسوبارا|vi|Matsubara, Ōsaka|war|Matsubara, Osaka|zh|松原市 (日本)|zh_classical|松原市 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Matubara-chhī|zh_yue|松原 (日本)|qid=Q774952}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. Its former rank was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

Along with {{ill|Shibagaki Shrine|Q11534936|qid=Q11534936}}, {{ill|Nunose Shrine|Q11480799|qid=Q11480799}}, Gadō Hachimangū, {{ill|Ao Shrine (Matsubara)|Q122900553|qid=Q122900553}} (all in Matsubara), and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amamikoso Shrine}} (Higashisumiyoshi-ku, Osaka), it forms the "Matsubara Six Shrines Fortune Pilgrimage"<ref>[https://matsubara-kanko.net/enjoy/rokusya/ Matsubara Six Shrines Pilgrimage] Matsubara Tourism Association</ref>.

=== History ===
It is said that in ancient times there was a Hohi shrine here enshrining {{ill|Ame no Hohi|lt=Ame-no-Hohi|Q10940685|qid=Q10940685|qid=Q10940685|lt=Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto}}, ancestral deity of the {{ill|Haji clan|Q10927758|qid=Q10927758}} (later {{ill|Sugawara clan|Q1771125|qid=Q1771125}}). According to the shrine document ''Miyake Tenmangū Baishōin Engi'', when Sugawara no Michizane was exiled to Dazaifu and passed through this land of his ancestors, he prayed at Hohi shrine and appealed his innocence<ref>[https://www.city.matsubara.osaka.jp/index.cfm/10,98,51,261,html Miyake Shrine and Tenjin worship - Matsubara City] viewed 2018-06-18</ref>. However, there are similar Michizane legends at places farther away in Osaka as well, and the full historical truth is unclear.

For direct history connected to the present shrine, it is said that in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Suzaku|Q361019|qid=Q361019}}, a monk named Dōken received an oracle of Eleven-faced Kannon and cooperated with locals to enshrine Michizane in 942 at Ira-Miyake-gō, Tanboku District, Kawachi Province<ref>[http://www12.plala.or.jp/HOUJI/jinja-1/newpage1207.htm Miyake Shrine - Rediscover Osaka!] viewed 2018-06-18</ref>. The site is also said to have been associated with the residence of the {{ill|Miyake clan|Q2975320|qid=Q2975320}}, a local warrior group of the {{ill|Hatakeyama clan|Q662881|qid=Q662881}}. In modern times, from around the Meiji period, the name shifted from Miyake Tenmangū to Miyake Shrine.

=== Cultural properties ===
A near life-size statue of Sugawara no Michizane is installed in the honden as a sacred image{{refnest|group=注釈|overall height 99.7 cm, overall width 128.3 cm, knee span 78 cm.}}. Tradition says Michizane reflected himself in a mirror at Dazaifu, carved this image, and sent it to this place; generally, however, the torso is considered an early-modern work.

Other Tenjin-related cultural materials remain, including Konoe Nobuhiro's self-painted "Tōto Tenjin image," an image titled "Sugawara no Michizane portrait" said to be in the hand of Emperor Go-Yōzei, and Konoe Motohiro's calligraphic title "Namu Tenman Daijizaitenjin."

=== Precincts ===
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Miyake-dera}} - former {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}}. Now abolished.

=== Subsidiary shrines ===
There are subsidiary shrines including {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsu Shrine}}, Hiyoshi Shrine, Ōmononushi Shrine, Susanoo Shrine, Amaterasu Ōkami Shrine, Kotohira Shrine, and Ichikishima Shrine.

=== Sakaya Shrine ===
As a precinct shrine there is '''Sakaya Shrine'''. The deity is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsuhayahino-Mikoto}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} and originally stood at today's Matsubara-shi Miyakenaka 6-2-2, but in 1907 it was moved into Miyake Shrine precincts<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20160304112937/http://www.geocities.jp/engisiki/kawachi/html/041307-01.html Sakaya Shrine] viewed 2018-06-18</ref>.
